question: Which world-groups are assigned to niyati, kāla, rāga, and the vidyā-kalā pair?
premises: In niyati there is a group of ten Śaṅkaras.
In kāla there is a group of ten Śivas, forming a pair of cities.
In rāga there is the well-delighted world and the teacher-disciple city.
In the pair of vidyā and kalā further worlds are assigned.
inference: The tattvas niyati, kāla, rāga, and the vidyā-kalā pair each contain specific named world-groups in the spatial hierarchy.
uncertainties: The exact identity of the ten Śaṅkaras and ten Śivas is not specified in this verse.
plain_english: In the tattva of restriction there are ten Śaṅkara worlds; in time there are ten Śiva worlds, making two cities. In attachment there are the well-delighted world and the teacher-disciple city, and in the pair of knowledge and limited agency there are further worlds.
